blockers.title: Repeated work/rest can block completion at indicator bounds
evidence: packages/social-dynamics/indicators.ail applyOne: IndicatorDelta computes n=value+delta and returns InvalidPolicyEffect when n is outside the configured range; there is no clipping
packages/social-dynamics/tasks.ail finish: release and completed status are staged before applyEffects, but on error neither is returned/published
packages/social-dynamics/engine.ail drive: a failed complete returns Blocked with the previous state
examples/crew-lab/scenario.ail existing values start readiness at 50 and fatigue at 45/30; the new draft does not prescribe a new boundary strategy
blockers.causal_example: For an engineer starting at readiness 50, +20 completions produce 70 and 90, then a third completion attempts 110. The proposed third replacement module remains reserved and the project remains Working. Repeated fatigue/stress-reducing rest similarly eventually attempts a negative value.
blockers.requested_resolution: Specify a modern-only strategy before execution: e.g. reject unsafe starts with exact bounds and human-readable explanation, or define explicitly versioned bounded completion handling without changing legacy semantics. Include repeated rest at zero, work at readiness/morale 100, stop/refund, and slot/supply conservation controls. Ensure stock-exhaustion acceptance tests are achievable under the chosen strategy.
blockers.why_blocking: The lab is explicitly intended for continued fast iteration and promises repeat-work stock exhaustion plus resource release. Current source-backed kernel behavior does not guarantee those mechanics under the draft's static deltas.

strongest_objection: The design treats host range validation as sufficient for playable bounded indicators, but the existing host rejects rather than saturates; valid assignments can become uncompletable later.
suggestions: Record initial fatigue, stress, morale and readiness values in the design or implementation data evidence so end-to-end boundary cases are reproducible.

At 40x16, inspect the actual first frame to ensure persistent policy explanation still leaves space for the captain/context/action flow; unit text-presence checks alone do not establish visible onboarding.
